title: Shooting victim had 'ugly' history; SIU probing if incident was 'suicide by cop': [ONT Edition]
article: Steve Remian led a troubled life, but "always had anoptimistic outlook," an online friend recalls.
Remian, 38, died in a hail of police bullets early Saturday after he confronted officers who trailed him to a park in a fashionable Oakville neighbourhood.
"He was always very optimistic - that's the one thing that actually drew me to talk with him," said Lucia of Kleinburg, who met Remian in an online chat room.

Officials from the province's Special Investigations Unit seized a rifle at the shooting scene in Wedgewood Park, in southeast Oakville next to a school Remian once attended. It was there that police, who were following up a report of a man with a rifle outside a Tim Hortons coffee shop on Trafalgar Rd., had tracked Remian, who was driving a car with British Columbia licence plates.
Witnesses at the coffee shop said the man had threatened to harm himself and others.

In a brief confrontation shortly after 2 30 a.m., three officers fired shots at the man as he emerged from a car. Officials are probing whether Remian pointed his weapon at police to commit "suicide by cop," in which someone challenges police, forcing them to fire.
Remian, a former Oakville resident, had moved to British Columbia to get a new job, but lost it and returned to Ontario.

The name "Steve Remian" surfaced at the Robert "Willie" Pickton murder trial in New Westminster, B.C., last March, when jurors were told that Remian's name - with a Burnaby, B.C., address - was on the label of a suitcase packed into a box found in Pickton's workshop.
In April, jurors heard further evidence that DNA testing on two hairs found on a Hudson's Bay blanket removed from Pickton's motorhome linked one to Pickton, and the other to a "Steve Remian."

A source involved in the Oakville shooting investigation told the Star that the man shot by police had been charged with sexual assault earlier in life while living in Oakville, but had been acquitted, although a co-accused was convicted.
"He had a pretty ugly family history," the source said.
Rose Bliss of the SIU said three officers, not four, fired their guns. It was the first fatal shooting involving Halton Region officers.
